coverage: Pre-market, Mon Nov 16 (covers Fri Nov 13 close to Mon Nov 16 pre-market)
moodReason: The S&P 500 still posted its first weekly gain since early October, but hot October inflation lifted Treasury yields and the AI chip selloff is weighing on tech. A busy earnings and data week, led by Nvidia on Tuesday, will decide which side wins.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down as board probes reports of a foreign intelligence effort; earnings due Tuesday
stories.what: Nvidia's board opened an internal investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, and Huang has stepped down. Colette Kress, the longtime CFO, is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia shares fell again on Friday and more than $600 billion of market value was wiped out that week. Nvidia reports quarterly results Tuesday after the close, its first report without Huang.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest weight in the AI trade, so its leadership turmoil and any guidance change on Tuesday can move the whole tech sector and the Nasdaq. Consensus expects about $2.49 EPS and roughly $108.8 billion in revenue, so a miss or cautious outlook would add pressure.

stories.headline: Hot October CPI keeps inflation in focus and pushes Treasury yields higher
stories.what: The October consumer price index rose 0.4% month over month, above the 0.3% forecast, after a 0.6% gain in September. Core CPI rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, the third straight monthly gain of that size. Average hourly earnings were up 3.1% from a year earlier, below the roughly 4% inflation pace. Yields rose after the report, with the 10-year near 5.15% and the 2-year at 4.87% on Friday.
stories.why: Sticky core inflation keeps the Federal Reserve from cutting and raises the chance of a hike, which lifts borrowing costs and compresses valuations for high-multiple growth stocks.

stories.headline: Traders weigh a possible December rate hike ahead of the Dec 8 to 9 Fed meeting
stories.what: Market commentary this week discusses the chance that the Federal Reserve raises rates at its December meeting, with a hike seen as more possible after hot inflation. The Fed meets December 8 and 9, and the November CPI report is due December 10, the day after the decision.
stories.why: A shift from expected cuts to a possible hike would tighten financial conditions, which pressures valuations and raises the bar for stocks to keep rising into year end.

stories.headline: Stocks end Friday mixed but post first winning week since early October
stories.what: The S&P 500 closed at 7,561.67, down 0.4% on Friday but up 2.5% for the week. The Dow rose 0.1% to 52,347.55 and gained 2.1% for the week. The Nasdaq fell 0.9% to 25,136.27 on the AI pullback, while the Russell 2000 slipped 0.3% to 2,790.49 and gained 1.3% for the week.
stories.why: The weekly gain shows the broad market held up despite the AI and Nvidia selloff, so the tone going into the week is more resilient than Friday's tape suggests.

stories.headline: Home Depot, Target and Walmart report this week as investors look for a read on the consumer
stories.what: Home Depot reports Tuesday before the open with consensus EPS of about $3.87. Target reports Wednesday before the open. Walmart reports Thursday before the open with consensus EPS of about $0.64. October retail sales, due Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, are expected to rise 0.2% after a 0.8% gain in September.
stories.why: With inflation running hot, retailer guidance and the retail sales print will show whether consumers are still spending. Weak numbers would support the rate-cut case, while strong spending would add to hike fears.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO expected to start trading Thursday, a test for AI sentiment
stories.what: Shares of Anthropic are expected to begin trading on Thursday, November 19, according to a week-ahead preview. The listing is being watched as a gauge of appetite for AI companies after the recent chip selloff.
stories.why: A strong debut could revive AI risk appetite, while a weak one could reinforce the bubble concerns that have hit AI chip shares since early October.

watch.item: Home Depot earnings before the open; Nvidia earnings after the close
October retail sales at 8:30 a.m. ET
Target earnings before the open; FOMC minutes at 2:00 p.m. ET
Congressional closed-door briefing with Jensen Huang requested by House Republicans
Walmart earnings before the open; Anthropic IPO expected to start trading
Federal Reserve meeting, with a possible rate hike in play

bottomLine: Stocks finished a rough Friday slightly lower but still gained about 2.5% on the S&P 500 for the week, so the market is holding up better than the headlines suggest. The main pressures are hot October inflation, rising Treasury yields, and the leadership shock at Nvidia, which has been the bellwether for the AI trade. This week's Nvidia, Home Depot, Target and Walmart reports and the retail sales data will show whether the economy can absorb higher rates.
